html:
Jože Plečnik was a Slovene architect, born in 1872 in Ljubljana, who reshaped his home city and the Prague Castle.

He trained in Vienna under Otto Wagner and built churches and houses there. From 1920 he renovated Prague Castle for President Masaryk. Back in Ljubljana he spent decades turning it into a national capital: the Triple Bridge, the riverside market, the embankments of the Ljubljanica and the National and University Library. His style mixed classical columns with folk touches. His Ljubljana works were added to the World Heritage list in 2021. Plečnik shows how Slovenia built a capital before it had a state.
